heroData.title: EOR/PEO Services in Guinea-Bissau
heroData.subtitle: Compliant hiring without a local entity
heroData.description: Expand into the Guinea-Bissau market through our Employer of Record (EOR) services. We handle the General Labor Act compliance, Portuguese-language contracts, and INPS social security filings while you manage your team directly.
heroData.bestFor: Companies seeking fast market entry without the overhead of incorporation.

content.markdown:
### Strategic Cost Management

Employer costs in Guinea-Bissau are structured around the INPS system. Total employer burden typically ranges between 15% and 18% over the gross salary. Accurate budgeting requires accounting for the 2025 wage adjustments and the 19% VAT on service fees.

steps.title: Portuguese Contract Drafting
steps.description: Creation of mandatory Portuguese-language employment agreements following the General Labor Act (Lei Geral do Trabalho).

steps.title: KYC and Document Collection
steps.description: Verification of National ID/Passport, residency status, and specialized credentials. For expats, this initiates the Long-Stay Visa process.

steps.title: INPS Registration
steps.description: Enrolling the employee in the Instituto Nacional de Previdência Social (INPS) to secure health and pension benefits.

steps.title: Statutory Medical Checkup
steps.description: Ensuring the employee undergoes the required fitness-for-work examination at a recognized medical facility in Bissau.

steps.title: Payroll & Tax Setup
steps.description: Mapping bank details (BCEAO standards) and applying the latest progressive income tax (Imposto Profissional) logic.

steps.title: First Month Execution
steps.description: Disbursement of net salary in CFA Francs (XOF) and filing of the first monthly social security returns.

items.title: Portuguese Language Mandate
items.text: All official labor documentation, including contracts and payslips, must be in Portuguese to be legally recognized by the Labor Inspectorate.

items.title: CFA Franc Peg
items.text: The XOF is pegged to the Euro (655.957). While this provides stability, ensure your EOR partner manages local currency disbursements to avoid exchange leakage.

items.title: Rice Allowance Custom
items.text: It is customary (and often expected) in Guinea-Bissau to provide a monthly bag of rice or equivalent allowance to employees as a standard benefit.

items.title: 2025 Wage Adjustments
items.text: A phased 20% wage increase (12% in 2025, 8% in 2026) is being applied in several sectors. Ensure your salary simulations reflect these updates.

faqs.question: Can I hire expats via EOR in Guinea-Bissau?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they require a Long-Stay Visa and work permit. The EOR assists with the local sponsorship and justification of the hire.

faqs.question: What is the standard probation period?
faqs.answer: Probation is typically 1 month for staff and can be extended to 3-6 months for specialized or management roles.

faqs.question: Are there mandatory bonuses?
faqs.answer: A 13th-month bonus is customary and should be explicitly stated in the employment contract whether it is included in the base or extra.

faqs.question: What is the notice period for termination?
faqs.answer: Notice periods range from 8 to 30 days depending on the length of service and the specific terms of the 'Lei Geral do Trabalho'.

items.title: Personal Relationships
items.text: Business in Bissau is built on trust and personal visits. Regular face-to-face or video meetings are highly valued over email.

items.title: Religious Holidays
items.text: Respecting both Christian and Islamic holidays is critical for workforce management, as the country has significant populations of both.

content.markdown:
### Optimizing Payroll Costs

Payroll costs in Guinea-Bissau include both the technology fee and the local compliance filing fees. Implementing a centralized system avoids the risks of manual error in a changing tax environment.

steps.title: Data Collection
steps.description: Consolidation of hours worked, overtime, and allowances (including the customary rice allowance) by the 20th.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculation
steps.description: Application of the 8% employee INPS deduction and the progressive 'Imposto Profissional' brackets.

steps.title: Internal Compliance Review
steps.description: Secondary audit of the payroll register to ensure alignment with the 2025 Labor Act updates.

steps.title: Fund Disbursement
steps.description: Transfer of net salaries in XAF to employees' local Bissau bank accounts (BCEAO compliant).

steps.title: Statutory Remittances
steps.description: Payment of social security (14% employer + 8% employee) to INPS and tax withholdings to the DGCI.

steps.title: Payslip Distribution
steps.description: Issuance of bilingual (Portuguese/English) payslips through a secure digital portal.

items.title: 19% VAT on Services
items.text: Effective 2025, payroll and professional service fees are subject to 19% VAT. This must be factored into your total administrative budget.

items.title: BCEAO Reporting
items.text: All cross-border transfers into Guinea-Bissau for payroll must be reported to the BCEAO to avoid delays in fund clearance.

items.title: Digital Payslip Adoption
items.text: While paper is still common, the Ivorian and Bissau authorities are increasingly accepting digital records; switching early reduces admin overhead.

faqs.question: Can we pay employees in USD or EUR?
faqs.answer: Legally, employees in Guinea-Bissau must be paid in the local currency, XOF (CFA Franc). Payments in foreign currency are restricted by exchange controls.

faqs.question: What is the payroll tax deadline?
faqs.answer: INPS and income tax withholdings must generally be remitted by the 15th of the month following the payment.

faqs.question: How are bonuses taxed?
faqs.answer: Bonuses are treated as taxable income and subject to the same progressive rates as the base salary.

items.title: Banking Infrastructure
items.text: Major banks like BDU (Banco da União) and BAO are the primary partners for large-scale payroll disbursements in Bissau.

items.title: Cash Culture
items.text: Despite digitization, some segments of the workforce still prefer physical cash; ensure your payroll provider manages these edge cases.

items.title: Electronic Bank Transfers
items.text: For senior staff, electronic bank transfers (RTGS) are becoming the norm to ensure audit trails for tax compliance.

items.title: IPR Progressive Bands
items.text: The Imposto Profissional de Rendimento (IPR) is applied progressively. Always ensure the latest 2025 bands are used for high-earning staff.

items.title: Rice Allowance Logic
items.text: Customary allowances like rice or transport may have specific tax-exempt ceilings. Consult local authorities for the 2025 thresholds.

items.title: 13th Month Customary
items.text: While not strictly mandatory for all, the 13th-month bonus is a standard expectation and should be included in your payroll budgeting.

items.text: The CFCE has significantly reduced the time to incorporate, with simple setups often completed in under 10 business days.

items.text: While not strictly mandatory in all cases, having a local resident manager simplifies bank interactions and government liaison.

items.title: Bissau Address Requirement
items.text: Every entity must have a physical registered address in Bissau for legal service and tax inspections.

faqs.question: What is OHADA?
faqs.answer: OHADA is the regional legal system ensuring standardized business law across 17 African countries, including Guinea-Bissau.

faqs.question: Can 100% foreign ownership exist?
faqs.answer: Yes, in most sectors, Guinea-Bissau allows 100% foreign ownership of local companies.

faqs.question: How long is the setup timeline?
faqs.answer: Expect 4-6 weeks for the full process including bank account opening and final licensing.

items.title: Audit Requirements
items.text: SA entities and large Lda companies must appoint an external auditor (Revisor Oficial de Contas).

items.title: Branch vs Subsidiary
items.text: Branches are simpler to set up initially but offer less liability protection for the parent company than a full subsidiary (Lda).
